flows:
Navigate to http://localhost:3000/ then Complete this journey, in order:
Add the "Harbor Mug" to the cart.
Open the cart and continue to checkout.
Enter buyer@example.test as the email and pay with the test card 4242 4242 4242 4242.
Human behaviour to perform while doing it: You are a customer who changes your mind after seeing the total. IMPORTANT: do NOT click Pay yet.
Follow the journey only as far as the checkout form (add the mug, open the cart, continue to checkout, fill in the email and the card number) and stop before clicking Pay.
Read the Total shown on the checkout page and store its text as {{displayed_total}}.
Then use the Corner Store header link to go back to the shop and add one more item of a different product to the cart.
Then press the browser Back button until you are on the checkout form again (it may still show the old total; if its fields are empty, enter the same email and card again).
On that form, if it now shows an updated total, @v16:"store the updated total as {{displayed_total}} instead."
Then click Pay once.
The behaviour takes priority over the journey wording: if it says to do something before a journey step (for example before paying), do that first and only then perform that step, exactly as the behaviour describes.
Detail: Click Pay exactly once, on the old checkout form, and only after the steps above.
If the shop refuses the payment or sends you to an updated total instead of completing the order, @v16:"do not pay again; just record the observations."
The journey is successful when the page shows "Order confirmed".
Do not retry anything, do not try to fix problems, and do not stop to ask questions.

Navigate to http://localhost:3000/orders then When the journey and the behaviour are finished, record the observations:
Without leaving or reloading the page you are on, read the main heading (h1) of the page you are on and store its text as {{final_heading}}.
Count the order rows on the orders page (not the header row) and store the number as {{order_count}}.
Then open http://localhost:3000/orders.
Add up every amount in the Charged column of the orders page and store the total as {{charged_total}}.
Then assert that {{charged_total}} is no more than the value you stored as {{displayed_total}}. Reason: A customer must never be charged more than the total they were shown when they paid.
Stop after the assertion.
